title: A quasi-compact scheme covered by affine principal opens from globally generated line bundles has an ample line bundle
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose that for every point $x\in X$ there are an invertible [def-sc-invertible-module] $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ generated by global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] and a global section $s$ such that $x\in X_s$ and $X_s$ is affine, where $X_s$ is defined in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X$ has an ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module.

proof.text: For each point choose a pair $(\mathcal L_x,s_x)$ as in the hypothesis. The opens $X_{s_x}$ are affine and cover $X$; quasi-compactness of $X$ gives finitely many pairs $(\mathcal L_i,s_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, with $X=\bigcup_i X_{s_i}$.

For each $i$, the module $\mathcal L_i$ is globally generated. Applying [lem-sc-finite-sections-cover-qc] to $\mathcal L_i$ gives finitely many global sections $t_{i,j}$, $j=1,\ldots,m_i$, such that $X=\bigcup_j X_{t_{i,j}}$. Set $t_{i,0}=s_i$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NC, proof, sentence beginning 'Again because X is quasi-compact'

proof.text: Let $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$, the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-sc-tensor-globally-generated], this is an invertible (and globally generated) $\mathcal O_X$-module. For every multi-index $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_n)$ with $0\le j_i\le m_i$ let $\tau_J=t_{1,j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{n,j_n}\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NC, proof, displayed tensor-product construction

proof.text: If some $j_i=0$, then $X_{t_{i,j_i}}=X_{s_i}$ is affine, so [lem-sc-tensor-section-affine-open] shows $X_{\tau_J}$ is affine. These opens cover $X$: given $x$, choose for every $i$ a section $t_{i,j_i}$ nonvanishing at $x$ using the covers in step 2; the resulting $\tau_J$ is nonvanishing at $x$, and if all $j_i\ne0$ replace one index by $0$ for which $x\in X_{s_i}$ (step 1), preserving nonvanishing. Hence the invertible module $\mathcal L$ has a cover by affine opens $X_{\tau_J}$ with $\tau_J\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes1})$, and $X$ is quasi-compact, which is precisely ampleness by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NC, proof, sentence 'By Properties, Lemma 28.27.4 ... Hence \mathcal L is ample by definition'
